why: The curation undone: the duel board advertised wherever it mechanically passes. This is the mutation the shipped validators CANNOT catch, and that is the whole reason it is pinned here -- vs-duel-01 measures suitable at N=3 and N=4 (versus-board.test.ts sweeps all 18 combinations and finds 18), so `versusCatalogEntryFailures` returns clean on the widened declaration and the schema accepts it. Before this branch the catalog's own test asserted every entry declared [2,3,4], so the widened form was the CONFORMING one. The ruling it breaks is that the offer is curated rather than derived: a board designed as a duel is withheld at counts where it is playable but not designed for. `declares the player counts each entry is CURATED for, not merely the ones it passes at` and `cross-check: everything offered is measured suitable, and what is withheld is named` are the cases that measure it, in two different files, from the catalog side and the menu side. Scoped to versus-catalog.test.ts; expectFailures counts that scoped run only. RE-ANCHORED for issue #272: this entry's find string used to run from `players` to the CLOSING BRACKETS OF THE FILE, which only matched while vs-duel-01 was the last catalog entry. Appending vs-tri-01 after it made the string absent and the harness reported failed-to-apply -- correctly, and it is the only thing that would have. The anchor is now the `players` block alone, which is unique to this entry (the five campaign boards declare [2,3,4] and vs-tri-01 declares [3]) and does not depend on position in the file.
killedBy: VERSUS_CATALOG declares the player counts each entry is CURATED for, not merely the ones it passes at
